answer: Stop a clone army with a juniper hedge on a trellis of routes. Each identity grows one juniper: endorsements from peers who have never endorsed each other, so copying a hedge needs a fresh peer set. Influence moves only across the trellis, and each act must send an echo that returns by a different trellis route, as a replay check. If N identities share a hedge root or an echo route, the protocol folds them into one identity, caps their joint influence at one share, and slashes each bond by the folded set size, so N clones stake N bonds for one share and face a loss near N times N when caught.
